q: What enters the write path: explicit agent-authored memories, or automatic extraction from interaction evidence?
a: only explicit MCP calls create/update memory; create_memory requires parent URI, content, priority, disclosure, and title, while no transcript-ingestion or candidate-extraction API exists (backend/mcp_server.py:390-456).

q: Is a memory primarily free text in an addressable graph, or a typed epistemic claim with evidence?
a: a memory is content plus graph placement metadata; the schema has no semantic type/tier/evidence/provenance/status fields (backend/db/models.py:95-110, backend/db/models.py:114-168).

q: Should third-party and sensitive material be structurally blocked, filtered after extraction, or left to the writer?
a: unrestricted text enters Memory.content; the write validation checks priority/disclosure/title and edit shape, not subject or person (backend/db/models.py:104-109, backend/mcp_server.py:457-480, backend/mcp_server.py:562-700).

q: Is the stable identity the claim, its location, or an underlying concept independent of both?
a: stable identity is a UUID Node; content versions and paths can change around it (backend/db/models.py:73-100).

q: On update, overwrite in place or append a version and supersede the old one?
a: append a new Memory, deprecate all active versions, link them via migrated_to, then activate the new row (backend/db/graph.py:1520-1544).

q: What happens on duplicate path, duplicate relation, or duplicate content?
a: duplicate (namespace,domain,path) is rejected by the path primary key; duplicate parent→child relation is prevented by a unique constraint; aliases intentionally point multiple paths to the

q: If deleting a path would orphan descendants, reject, cascade-delete, or auto-heal?
a: preserve content where possible; removal may rehome descendant paths under a surviving alias, disambiguate collisions with UUID suffixes, or reject when no safe route exists

q: Who resolves contradictions: last write, explicit correction, accumulation, or user confirmation?
a: update_memory creates a newest active version; migration cleanup selects latest timestamp/ID when multiple active versions exist (backend/db/graph.py:1520-1544, backend/db/migrations/007_v1.1.0_enforce_single_active_memory.py:13-16). The store does not identify semantic contradiction.

q: Retrieve by explicit address, lexical relevance, graph neighborhood, semantic similarity, or all of them?
a: explicit URI reads traverse direct children; search is lexical FTS over path, URI, content, disclosure, and glossary-derived terms; there are no embeddings (backend/db/graph.py:251-361, backend/db/search.py:279-391, backend/db/migrations/009_v1.3.0_add_search_fts.py:16-21).

q: How are results ordered, and where does priority enter?
a: children order by lower edge priority then name; search orders by FTS score, then lower priority, then shorter path; duplicate aliases collapse to the first

q: Is disclosure a machine-enforced permission or a human-readable hint to the caller?
a: disclosure is free text on an edge, included in formatted reads/search results; no policy engine interprets it (backend/db/models.py:127-130, backend/db/search.py:379-388, backend/mcp_server.py:401-403).

q: What is exposed to callers: raw content, metadata, graph context, evidence, or an explanation trace?
a: a read returns content, memory ID, priority, disclosure, aliases/children, and glossary references; search returns URI, snippet, priority, disclosure (backend/mcp_server.py:297-303, backend/system_views.py:21-164, backend/mcp_server.py:1048-1066).

q: On missing data or low confidence, return an error/empty set, ask, abstain with trace, or guess?
a: missing URI and invalid input become text beginning Error:; empty search returns “No memories found”; the storage system has no confidence score and cannot distinguish

access timestamps/logs change on reads; diagnostic staleness changes with time; no content decays, expires, promotes, or demotes automatically (backend/db/graph.py:76-93, backend/db/models.py:227-243, backend/db/graph.py:438-524, backend/db/models.py:95-110).

q: What is assumed idempotent or ordered?
a: create is not idempotent: an occupied path errors; update of an already-active rollback target reports was_already_active; snapshot recording is order-sensitive—first before is frozen and later

q: Is multi-user separation a namespace column, separate database, or authorization boundary?
a: namespace scopes paths, glossary, search, access logs, and presets, while nodes/memories/edges are shared underlying identities (backend/db/models.py:145-168, backend/db/models.py:171-224, backend/db/models.py:227-260). Middleware obtains namespace from environment/header/query transport (backend/namespace_middleware.py:11-18).
